messages:
deploy-bot: Alert: Canary group 'sdk-release-3.5' is showing elevated 5xx (service-stream) at 2143657889. Canary health degraded to 18%. Auto-rollout paused.

Eva (oncall): I see the canary error spikes — reproducing locally against canary image gives streaming handshake fails.

Mike (eng): quick summary: SDK v3.5 changed paging token serialization from JSON+base64 -> raw urlsafe base64 string. Server side expects old JSON-wrapped token for streaming rehydrate; mismatch causes token parser to return 400 and abort stream.

Alex (ops): Confirmed via ingress logs:
```
ingress-proxy[xyz]: 400 GET /v1/stream?paging_token=eyJ... - "InvalidPagingToken: expected map"
service-stream[abc]: panic: could not parse paging token: invalid character 'e' in string literal
```

Eva (oncall): That matches. Customer-facing streams dropping, some retry loops causing higher CPU. Impact: ~3% of active sessions interrupted (canary region eu-west).

pm-sam: Any customer-visible errors in the dashboard? We need to prepare comms if rollback takes long.

Mike (eng): Root cause in SDK: when token is serialized as plain urlsafe base64, the server's token decoder does `json.Unmarshal` directly on the token payload assuming it's the old object format. New format wraps differently. Fix options: server-side tolerant decoder OR revert SDK.

Alex (ops): Mitigation preference? Can we flip a feature flag on the API gateway to accept both formats quickly?

Mike (eng): There's a feature flag gate in parsing code but it was removed in the canary for perf. Quickest safe action: flip canary traffic back to 3.4 and enable kill switch for new-paging-header enforcement so we stop issuing new tokens in canary.

Eva (oncall): I'll do immediate mitigation — kill new paging header issuing and rollback canary. Starting steps now.

Alex (ops): Running: `kubectl -n infra exec deploy-gateway -- /bin/sh -c "redis-cli set ff:sdk_new_paging_header 0"`
Operation result: OK

Alex (ops): Gateway logs show flag read: `ff:sdk_new_paging_header=0` and now new outgoing tokens are back to legacy JSON format.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated for deployment sdk-release-3.5 -> previous replicaSet (3.4). Rollout started at 2143658002.

Mike (eng): Good. Also pushing a draft server-side tolerant parser patch that tries to detect raw urlsafe base64 vs json-wrapped token and reject gracefully instead of crashing. Will open PR now: `github.com/redwood/service-stream/pull/472`

se-jordan: For customer impact, we should send an FYI to customers with active streaming integrations in eu-west. pm-sam you ok with short note explaining temporary disruption and rollback?

pm-sam: Yes. Drafting message: "We rolled back SDK canary after detecting a paging token format mismatch that impacted streaming sessions. We reverted to the previous SDK behavior and applied a gateway kill-switch. No auth/data exposure. Follow-up patch to improve server tolerance is in progress."

Eva (oncall): Canary rollback completed at 2143658150. Health back to normal for canary group. 5xx rate back to baseline.

Alex (ops): Confirming metrics: CPU dipped 12%, error budget stable. No ongoing retries.

Mike (eng): PR opened and added unit test for both token formats. Will coordinate with SDK team to cut SDK 3.5.1 with token encoded to legacy shape by default and add opt-in header for new format.

Arya (oncall): I'm taking over the shift from Eva. Eva handing off: all mitigations applied, rollback complete, monitoring on alert thresholds. Roadmap: follow up on tolerant parser and SDK patch tomorrow morning.

Eva (oncall): Handover ack. Key action items: 1) Mike to land tolerant parser PR + deploy to staging; 2) SDK team to cut 3.5.1 with revert or backward-compatible token; 3) pm-sam to send customer comms; 4) postmortem runbook scheduled.

pm-sam: Customer FYI sent to affected customers at 2143658260.

Mike (eng): Quick note for postmortem: include decision tree that allowed parser removal in canary and add gate checklist for protocol changes (contract bump requires server feature flag at least one release behind).

deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2143657890. Assigned: Mike, Alex, Eva. Priority: P1 -> downgraded to P2 after rollback.

Arya (oncall): Taking over monitoring. If we see >1% session error rate for 15m, I'll re-open the incident. Otherwise will convert to follow-up RFC.

se-jordan: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick rollback and composable mitigation (flag + rollback). We'll sync tomorrow for postmortem and release plan. :thumbsup:
